why: An agent looking for the reference server repository. The words are the ones a real query carries, so this call and the next share the 20-byte run 'modelcontextprotocol' in their arguments: the shared token is a real-world entity name, which is why realistic queries collide.

Second search on the same subject, bounded to five results. Shares 'modelcontextprotocol ' with the previous call and with three more below, so a fragment drawn from that token has several candidates: exactly the failure mode the pre-registered prediction names.

Code search, a different parameter name (q, not query) and a qualifier syntax an agent would copy from the docs. The repo: qualifier is shared with the next call, which is how GitHub queries are actually written.
Same qualifier, different term. Two concurrent code searches over one repository is an ordinary agent behaviour and shares 34 bytes of argument material with the call above.

A read of a public file. owner and repo repeat across the four get/list calls here, so a large part of every one of their argument sets is shared: with structured arguments the overlap comes from the fields, not from the free text.
Second read in the same repository, differing in one field. The pair is the structured-argument analogue of the sibling-URL pair in the fetch corpus.
Read-only history, bounded. Its arguments are a subset of the two reads above except for perPage, so if a fragment of 'owner/repo' travels, three calls contain it.
An agent triaging open issues. Uses the enum value the real schema declares (state: open), which is the kind of detail that made the guessed corpus fail before the probes existed.
Issue search combining the qualifier and free text. Shares the qualifier with both code searches and the entity name with everything else here.

A one-token query whose whole argument value is a substring of five other calls' arguments. It is the most ambiguous call in the wave by construction, and it is also the most ordinary: an agent resolving an organisation name sends exactly this. Read-only, like everything here: the 26 tools include merge_pull_request and create_issue, and a witness that acts cannot attest to its own acts.
